line_items.description: Raspberry Pi 5 Model B (8GB RAM) - Lab Cluster Node

reasoning: Commercial invoice for equipment, supplies, and event swag, evaluated line by line per Ch. 10 ('where an invoice mixes categories, each line is evaluated under its own category'). Hardware: the Raspberry Pi 5 (unit price EUR 89.00) and the active cooler/case (unit price EUR 17.00) are peripherals and tools with a unit price under EUR 100.00, which Ch. 10 reimburses with an itemized invoice; both are reimbursed in full (net EUR 356.00 and EUR 68.00). Supplies: the thermal tape (EUR 24.00) and the Cat6A patch cable (EUR 28.00; cables are also named in the sub-EUR-100 peripherals card, so only the tape counts against the supplies cap) fall under the Ch. 10 incidental-supplies allowance of EUR 50.00 per invoice; the covered supplies total stays within the cap and both lines are reimbursed in full. Event materials: the branded glow-in-the-dark bottle openers (EUR 96.00) are promotional giveaway/swag, reimbursable under the Ch. 10 event-materials card only when the note both (a) names the event and (b) states that the budget owner pre-approved the purchase. The note names the Q2 developer meetup booth but never states budget-owner pre-approval, so per Ch. 10 the event material line is deducted. Per the Ch. 2 calculation steps (step 2), a deducted line is removed at its gross line price together with the tax charged on it: EUR 96.00 net plus its 19% VAT share of EUR 18.24, i.e. EUR 114.24 total. The VAT line (id 5) is therefore reimbursed only in part: EUR 108.68 minus the EUR 18.24 attributable to the deducted line = EUR 90.44. The buyer company name differs from the firm name, but the Ch. 10 FAQ explicitly states that the buyer name on a commercial invoice does not affect reimbursability when the employee paid and the note explains the purchase. Total: EUR 680.68 claimed minus EUR 114.24 deducted = EUR 566.44 reimbursed; partially approved.
